subject: Canary failover spike — request for SLA eligibility & postmortem
messages:
From: BlueHarbor Ops <ops@blueharbor.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T03:12:00Z
Subject: sudden 503/authorization failures affecting checkout (aug 15)

Hey Dylan —

We saw a ~7 minute window this morning (02:47–02:54 UTC) where ~20% of /v1/generate calls returned 503 or an authorization fallback response. This hit our checkout flow and we had to toggle to retry logic; estimated revenue impact for that window is ~2.3k USD.

Attached are a compressed bundle with client-side logs and sampled traces (bh-client-logs.tar.gz). Can Redwood confirm whether that maps to a server-side availability window eligible for SLA credit? We need:

- confirmation of an availability gap window and start/end timestamps;
- whether the canary failover you mentioned in last week's notice was active in our region at the time;
- a quick plan for the postmortem and expected timeline for evidence.

Please loop in the person who will own the postmortem and any compensation steps.

Thanks,
Sam Chang
Site Reliability Engineer — BlueHarbor
ops@blueharbor.com

Attachment: bh-client-logs.tar.gz (application/gzip)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: BlueHarbor Ops <ops@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T04:05:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 503/authorization failures affecting checkout (aug 15)

Sam —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the logs. We're opening an incident ticket on our side (INC-9427) to correlate service telemetry. Initial ask: can you confirm the customer request IDs / example request payloads (X-Req-Id) for a couple of failed calls so we can tie them to token buckets and routing decision traces? That accelerates our KV-cache/route-level tracing.

Quick answers up front:
- We had a scheduled canary promotion in us-west-2 at 02:30–03:00 UTC for an authorization routing change; it should have had automatic safe-guards but we'll validate whether Canary -> Primary routing misapplied to your traffic.
- We will prioritize evidence pull (raw trace spans + host-level logs) and return a proposed downtime window and eligibility statement by EOD US.

I'll coordinate internal ownership — tagging Karthik to lead the SLO eligibility check and Laura for postmortem scope.

Next steps (internal):
- Karthik: confirm start/end and severity classification; provide initial eligibility assessment.
- Laura: scope postmortem and timeline for a customer-facing RCA.

Sam, expected timeline from us: preliminary eligibility reply within 8 hours, full postmortem draft within 72 hours. If that timeline won't work for you, tell me what you need.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: (none)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 503/authorization failures affecting checkout (aug 15) — initial findings

Team —

I pulled the control-plane and serving logs for INC-9427. Summary of what I see:

- Windows: 2026-08-15T02:46:58Z -> 2026-08-15T02:54:35Z (7m37s) where 503/authorization fallback rate to BlueHarbor requests increased from baseline 0.3% to 19.8%.
- Root cause (preliminary): an incomplete rollback during a canary promotion caused a small percentage of requests to be routed to a partially-initialized auth shim that returned 503s for certain token shapes.
- Affected infra: us-west-2 serving pool (pool-id: rw-usw2-3).

Evidence attached: sampled host logs (sampled-traces-08-15.ndjson) and a short timeline (bh-logs-20260815.tar.gz).

SLO/eligibility note: per our SLA (section 3.2) an availability gap > 99.9% for the region over a contiguous window qualifies for remediation review. This window appears to meet our internal threshold for a customer-eligible incident. I'll prepare a credit calculation (pro-rata) and pass to Dylan to confirm commercial next steps.

Proposed immediate mitigations we applied:
- forced routing stable candidate and disabled the promo flag at 02:55:10Z;
- applied a corrective hotfix to the canary promotion logic to avoid partial routes (deployed 03:08:00Z).

I'll draft the detailed timeline and include per-customer request counts so we can compute exact credit.

Karthik
Director, Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sampled-traces-08-15.ndjson (text/ndjson), bh-logs-20260815.tar.gz (application/gzip)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: BlueHarbor Ops <ops@blueharbor.com>, Samantha Wells <samantha.wells@acmepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T18:32:00Z
Subject: Canary routing incident — confirmation of window and next steps (INC-9427)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal incident investigation (INC-9427), we can confirm the availability gap that affected BlueHarbor as: 2026-08-15T02:46:58Z through 2026-08-15T02:54:35Z (UTC). Karthik's note above includes the trace and host-level evidence.

What we are proposing next:
1) SLA credit eligibility: Redwood will proceed with a pro-rata credit calculation for the affected billing period. Our commercial team will calculate the dollar amount and route a formal credit memo within 3 business days. (Deal: BH-3421)
2) Postmortem / customer-facing RCA: Laura will own the postmortem and deliver a draft customer-facing RCA in 72 hours, with the following focal points:
   - exact timeline and root cause analysis;
   - why the canary safety-guard did not prevent partial routing;
   - mitigations and scheduler changes to avoid recurrence;
   - verification plan to assert the fix.
3) Evidence bundle: attached are the raw traces and the sample logs we used to verify the window. If you have additional request IDs / payloads, send them and we will map them into the timeline.

Marissa (billing), can you prepare the credit memo draft and confirm any contractual constraints on crediting (we may need a signed acknowledgement from the customer to close the incident for accounting)?

Sam — does the proposed path and timeline work for BlueHarbor? If you prefer we open a joint postmortem call, Laura can host one tomorrow morning US time.

Appreciate the partnership and apologies for the impact. We'll prioritize remediation and ensure the credit process is transparent.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: bh-logs-20260815.tar.gz, sampled-traces-08-15.ndjson
